summary: The added `if M.shape[i] > 0:` guards are functionally a no-op: `for i in range(0)` already iterates zero times, so wrapping the loops changes nothing and does not alter the computed shape. The change neither fixes the reported dense Matrix.hstack/vstack shape bug (which lives in the matrix join code, not BlockMatrix.shape) nor prevents any IndexError, since the guards sit on the wrong dimension relative to the indexing `M[i,0]`/`M[0,i]`.

issues.description: Guards are ineffective. `if M.shape[0] > 0:` around `for i in range(M.shape[0]):` is redundant because range(0) is already empty; identical output for every input, including empty/zero-size blocks. Change has no behavioral effect.

Reported issue is Matrix.hstack/vstack (dense Matrix) returning (0,3) instead of (0,6). That path does not go through BlockMatrix.shape; root cause is in the row_join/col_join reduce logic. This diff cannot resolve the linked issue.
Even if intended defensively, guarding a loop that is already safe against zero-length ranges adds noise and misleads future readers into thinking an edge case is handled.
